clauses.reason: The sole operative sentence of Executive Order 8358 revokes Executive Order No. 4308 of September 23, 1925, which temporarily withdrew public lands in Arizona for classification pending examination of certain Indian ruins. A present-tense revocation with no later effective date is carried out when the order takes effect, so the command was exhausted by performance on the order's signing date, 1940-03-02, which is recorded as the end. The filing date March 4, 1940 and the issue date March 6, 1940 are the alternatives if effectiveness is dated from filing or publication. The Federal Register docket line shows filing on March 4, 1940 and the issue is dated March 6, 1940.

research_rationale:
Identity and text: the held original is the machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register issue (5 FR 950, PDF pages 2-3, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-1940-03-06/pdf/FR-1940-03-06.pdf, sha256 77ec83df6766949361cefdd69ade5de5a5cefb4746e6f71e496f416a7c05c4ac); the text layer is OCR, the page image is not held in the repository, and the order was identified from the text layer. The order's heading, subject, signature date and closing number tag appear together as one short order whose whole text is the clause. Inventory: one operative sentence revoking Executive Order No. 4308 of September 23, 1925, which temporarily withdrew public lands in Arizona for classification pending examination of certain Indian ruins; there is no other clause. End: a present-tense revocation is carried out when the order takes effect, and the order postpones nothing, so the command was exhausted by performance on its signing date 1940-03-02; the filing date March 4, 1940 and the issue date March 6, 1940 are the alternative dates if effectiveness is dated from filing or publication. Later instruments: the packet's later-events search of Office of the Federal Register disposition notes (1937 onward) and its current-law searches of the U.S. Code and the eCFR were selected after reading their coverage notes, and each returned no hit for this order. A later revocation or repeal of the order is not needed to end a command that was already performed.

savings.reason: The held text contains no savings or transition clause. Its single command, revocation of Executive Order No. 4308 of September 23, 1925, which temporarily withdrew public lands in Arizona for classification pending examination of certain Indian ruins, was completed when the order took effect. The revoked order's loss of effect is a completed consequence that survives as an accrued result, not as a continuing command of this order.
